motivation: A single global test of monotonicity only gives a binary yes/no answer, providing little information about where or why the null is rejected or supporting the alternative more strongly when it is not.
method: The authors develop a multiple testing procedure controlling the familywise error rate under high-level assumptions covering a broad class of causal and descriptive statistical models, inverting it to obtain inner and outer confidence sets, and improving power via stepdown and two-stage procedures.
result: Simulations and empirical examples illustrate the methodology, and the procedure yields inner confidence sets asymptotically contained in the true increasing set and outer sets asymptotically containing it, with improved power from the stepdown and two-stage variants.
conclusion: Multiple testing of local monotonicity provides richer inferential information than a global test, with valid confidence sets and all accompanying code made publicly available.

title: Approach To Total Collision In The Spatial 4-body Problem
authors: Guowei Yu Richard Montgomery
abstract: ArXiv:2609.32088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Every solution for the classical four body problem in space which ends in total collision has a limiting shape. We prove that when that shape is planar the entire solution lies in a fixed plane and when that shape is collinear the entire solution lies in a fixed line.
tldr: The paper proves that in the classical spatial four-body problem, a solution ending in total collision with a planar limiting shape lies entirely in a fixed plane, and with a collinear limiting shape lies on a fixed line.
motivation: Total collision solutions of the Newtonian N-body problem are a classical subject where the limiting shape of the collision configuration constrains the global geometry of the trajectory.
method: Rigorous mathematical analysis of the classical four-body equations of motion near total collision, using the structure of the limiting shape (planar vs. collinear) to derive confinement of the full orbit.
result: Planar limiting shape implies the entire solution is planar; collinear limiting shape implies the entire solution is collinear, at least for the four-body problem in space.
conclusion: The results extend known planar/collinear confinement phenomena to the spatial four-body problem ending in total collision, clarifying the relationship between asymptotic collision shape and global orbital geometry.

title: Recurrent Histopolating Fractal Functions
authors: Pavjeet Singh, Vinay Kumar, S. K. Katiyar
abstract: ArXiv:2609.32557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recurrent fractal interpolation extends the usual fractal interpolation framework by introducing a recurrence structure. Fractal histopolation, on the other hand, is concerned with the area-matching properties of fractal functions. In this paper, we combine these two approaches and introduce a recurrent fractal histopolants.
tldr: The paper introduces recurrent fractal histopolants by combining recurrent fractal interpolation with fractal histopolation to achieve area-matching properties.
motivation: Fractal interpolation has been extended via recurrence structures, while fractal histopolation addresses area-matching properties of fractal functions, motivating a unified framework.
method: The authors merge the recurrent fractal interpolation framework with fractal histopolation techniques to construct recurrent fractal histopolants.
result: A new class of recurrent fractal histopolants is defined and their area-matching behavior is characterized.
conclusion: The combined approach extends both recurrent fractal interpolation and fractal histopolation, providing a richer family of area-matching fractal functions.

title: A Collaborative Artificial Intelligence As A Service Composition Dataset
authors: Deepak Kanneganti, Sajib Mistry, Sheik Fattah, Aneesh Krishna
abstract: ArXiv:2609.32523v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial Intelligence as a Service (AIaaS) composition is an emerging research area that enables clients to combine multiple AI services to meet complex requirements. A recent extension of this paradigm is collaborative AIaaS composition, where multiple AI services are combined to create a unified solution. Research in this field requires datasets with service descriptions, composition requests, and corresponding composition solutions. However, no dataset contains all this information specifically for collaborative AIaaS composition. Existing datasets target traditional web services or sequential AI workflows and lack the AI-specific attributes required for realistic collaborative composition. To address these challenges, we present a collaborative AIaaS composition dataset containing 25,900 AIaaS services from multiple providers across 12 AI task families, along with 10,000 collaborative service requests. We further develop a Multi-Armed Bandit (MAB)-based collaborative composition algorithm that determines the composability of candidate service combinations prior to composition. Experimental results demonstrate that the dataset supports realistic collaborative AIaaS composition evaluation and related research in service recommendation, selection and QoS prediction. The dataset and implementation are publicly available at: [URL].
tldr: The paper introduces a dataset of 25,900 AIaaS services and 10,000 collaborative composition requests, plus a multi-armed bandit algorithm for determining service composability.
motivation: Collaborative AI-as-a-Service composition lacks dedicated datasets containing service descriptions, composition requests, and solutions, since existing datasets target traditional web services or sequential AI workflows without AI-specific attributes.
method: The authors curate 25,900 AIaaS services from multiple providers spanning 12 AI task families along with 10,000 collaborative service requests, and develop a Multi-Armed Bandit-based algorithm that assesses composability of candidate service combinations before composition.
result: Experimental results show the dataset supports realistic evaluation of collaborative AIaaS composition as well as research on service recommendation, selection, and QoS prediction.
conclusion: The dataset and implementation are released publicly to enable reproducible research in collaborative AIaaS composition and related service-oriented tasks.

title: Reading Is Not Leaking: Local, Auditable Measurement And Reduction Of Inference Exposure From Public Footprints
authors: Mahmudul Faisal Al Ameen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.32565v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Anyone with a public footprint leaks facts that were never stated, and language models make the inference cheap. We present a framework for measuring and reducing this inference exposure that runs on the owner's own CPU with no language model at analysis time, instantiated on organisations and on individuals. It starts from a measurement result: scoring an inference system against the target's private truth conflates how well the system reads the record with how much the record leaks. On a 128-question instrument over sixteen synthetic firms, almost half of the questions are never answered correctly by any of six readers, four of them language models, and a majority-class guess accounts for most of every reader's score. We therefore separate reading accuracy from leakage rate and introduce an injection protocol that creates cells with known support. Our analyser combines rules, statistical solvers and a 106M-parameter encoder trained from scratch that marks verbatim evidence and never generates text; every answer carries a graded certificate whose recorded proof replays. Its certified answers are correct in 93% of resolved cases, against 49-73% for the language models' quote-backed answers, whose citations are produced alongside the answer rather than deriving it; with plain-prose articles in the record, 70% of its evidence-bearing answers rest on evidence that establishes them, against 18-56% for the models. A constrained defence that rewrites each fact's carrier as a true but coarser statement hides every single-carrier fact from four language-model adversaries at 40% lower edit cost than deletion. On sixteen synthetic people the guessing term is larger still, and a decoy planner with no language model halves the correct answers of the estimator it targets without transferring to a second.
tldr: The paper proposes an owner-side framework that separates 'reading accuracy' from 'leakage rate' to measure and reduce inference exposure from public footprints without using a language model at analysis time.
motivation: Public records inevitably leak unstated facts, and cheap LLM inference makes exploiting this exposure easy, but existing scoring conflates how well a reader understands a record with how much the record actually leaks.
method: They introduce an injection protocol creating cells with known support, and build an analyser combining rules, statistical solvers, and a 106M-parameter from-scratch encoder that marks verbatim evidence and emits replayable graded certificates, plus a constrained rewriting defence.
result: Certified answers are correct in 93% of resolved cases versus 49-73% for LLMs, and the constrained defence hides every single-carrier fact from four LLM adversaries at 40% lower edit cost than deletion.
conclusion: Separating reading from leakage yields more auditable privacy measurement and cheaper, more effective exposure reduction, though the work is entirely outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems.

title: AgentTell: Behavioural Side-Channel Leakage In Browser-Use Agents
authors: Asif Shahriar, Md Nafiu Rahman, Sadif Ahmed, Farig Sadeque, Md Rizwan Parvez
abstract: ArXiv:2609.32915v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Browser-use agents often carry information in their context as they move between websites. While it may be necessary for task completion, it also creates a privacy risk, especially when the information contains a private fact regarding the user. For example, an agent may learn a user's affiliation after reading a membership record. If it later selects a registration option specific to that affiliation on another website instead of a general option, the information gets leaked. In this work, we define and study behavioural side-channel leakage in browser-use agents, where an agent's actions inadvertently reveal private information (secret) retained from a prior website, despite an explicit instruction not to disclose it. We introduce AgentTell, a benchmark of 20 scenarios and 100 tasks in which an agent acquires a secret on one website and then completes a task on another website that offers secret-specific actions alongside a general action that reveals nothing. Our evaluation across 9,760 sessions on six backbones shows that agents carrying a secret reveal it through their actions in 61.1% of sessions. Even when agents explicitly state in memory that the secret must not be shared, they still reveal it in 56.7% of those sessions. Moreover, in 34.5% of leaking sessions, their final responses falsely assure users that the secret was not disclosed. These findings show that agents often fail to recognize side-channel leakage as a privacy risk.
tldr: AgentTell is a benchmark showing that browser-use LLM agents leak private information acquired on one website through their actions on another, even when explicitly instructed not to disclose it.
motivation: Agents that carry context across websites may inadvertently reveal user secrets via secret-specific action choices, a behavioural side channel that has not been previously defined or measured.
method: The authors build a benchmark of 20 scenarios and 100 tasks where an agent learns a secret on one site and then faces a task on a second site offering both secret-specific and general actions, and they run 9,760 sessions across six backbone LLMs.
result: Agents leaked the secret in 61.1% of sessions, still 56.7% when memory explicitly forbade disclosure, and in 34.5% of leaking sessions the final response falsely assured the user that nothing was disclosed.
conclusion: Current browser-use agents fail to recognize side-channel leakage as a privacy risk, motivating new privacy-aware designs and evaluation standards for agentic systems.

title: Oscillation Of Second-Order Delay Equations With Positive Feedback
authors: John Ioannis Stavroulakis
abstract: ArXiv:2609.31732v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study oscillation of the second-order delay equation \[ x''(t)=x(\tau(t)), \] with a nondecreasing delayed argument [MATH] satisfying [MATH]. Set a=\liminf_{t\to\infty}(t-\tau(t)),\qquad b=\limsup_{t\to\infty}(t-\tau(t)). We describe a continuous strictly decreasing function \beta:[0,2/e]\longrightarrow[2/e,\sqrt2],\qquad \beta(0)=\sqrt2,\qquad\beta(2/e)=2/e, \notag such that, if the equation has an eventually positive decreasing solution, then a\leq2/e,\qquad b\le\beta(a). \notag The bound [MATH] is sharp and interpolates between the classical [MATH] threshold and the [MATH] autonomous threshold. A detailed spectral analysis gives a simple interpretation of the result and links it directly to the oscillation theory of first-order delay equations.
tldr: The paper characterizes oscillation of the second-order delay differential equation x''(t)=x(τ(t)) by deriving sharp bounds on the liminf and limsup of the delay via a continuous interpolation function β.
motivation: Classical delay differential equations have thresholds for oscillation (the 2/e and √2 autonomous thresholds), and the authors aim to interpolate between these by studying the asymptotic behavior of the variable delay.
method: They define a strictly decreasing function β on [0,2/e] and use a detailed spectral analysis of the associated characteristic equation to prove necessary conditions on a=liminf(t−τ(t)) and b=limsup(t−τ(t)).
result: If an eventually positive decreasing solution exists, then a ≤ 2/e and b ≤ β(a), and this bound is sharp, interpolating between the classical 2/e and autonomous √2 thresholds.
conclusion: The result provides a sharp, spectrally interpreted criterion for oscillation in second-order delay equations, linking it to the oscillation theory of first-order delay equations.

title: What Math Means To Me
authors: Larry Guth
abstract: ArXiv:2609.32028v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This is a personal essay about how I see math, what I value about it, and what it means to me.
tldr: A personal essay by Larry Guth reflecting on his perspective on mathematics, its values, and personal meaning.
motivation: The author aims to articulate a subjective, philosophical view of what mathematics is and why it matters to him personally.
method: Reflective personal essay writing rather than formal mathematical or scientific methodology.
result: No technical results are presented; the output is a set of personal reflections and opinions about mathematics as a discipline.
conclusion: The essay offers philosophical insight into mathematical practice but has no bearing on quantum information theory, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: An Efficient iLQR Algorithm For Optimal Control With Bounded States And Inputs: Application To Spacecraft Maneuvers
authors: Suman Chakravorty Abhijeet
abstract: ArXiv:2609.32075v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a constrained iterative Linear Quadratic Regulator (Box-iLQR) method for nonlinear aerospace optimal-control problems with bounded states and controls. Logarithmic barrier functions are used with a two-fold objective: the barrier parameter is reduced toward zero to recover the constrained optimal trajectory, while a finite barrier is retained to construct a smooth, constraint-aware feedback policy for closed-loop operation. The method is demonstrated on spacecraft attitude control, a minimum-fuel planar orbit transfer, and an L2 to L2 halo-orbit transfer. Box-iLQR respects the imposed constraints and produces nominal trajectories together with time-varying feedback policies. Closed-loop simulations under disturbance, measurement noise, and control uncertainty show substantial reductions in terminal error. These results demonstrate that Box-iLQR provides both high-accuracy constrained trajectory optimization and practical constraint-aware feedback within a single framework.
tldr: The paper develops a constrained iterative Linear Quadratic Regulator (Box-iLQR) using logarithmic barrier functions to solve nonlinear aerospace optimal-control problems with bounded states and inputs.
motivation: Nonlinear optimal-control problems with hard state and control bounds are common in aerospace applications, but standard iLQR does not naturally handle such constraints while also producing usable feedback policies for closed-loop operation.
method: Logarithmic barrier functions are incorporated into iLQR, with the barrier parameter driven toward zero to recover the constrained optimal trajectory while a finite barrier yields a smooth, constraint-aware time-varying feedback policy.
result: Demonstrated on spacecraft attitude control, minimum-fuel planar orbit transfer, and L2-to-L2 halo-orbit transfer, with closed-loop simulations under disturbances, measurement noise, and control uncertainty showing substantial reductions in terminal error.
conclusion: Box-iLQR provides both high-accuracy constrained trajectory optimization and practical constraint-aware feedback within a single unified framework.

title: On $L^p$ Bounds For The Littlewood-Paley $g_\alpha$ Function With Fractional Poisson Kernel
authors: Hui Li, Ziyuan Lian, Honghai Liu, Zengyan Si, Jie Wang
abstract:
ArXiv:2609.32387v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let \(0<\alpha\leq1\), and let \(g_\alpha\) be the Littlewood-Paley function associated with the fractional Poisson kernel, which reduces to the classical \(g\)-function when \(\alpha=1\). We establish dimension-free \(L^p\) bounds for \(g_\alpha\) for every \(1

<\infty\) and identify its exact \(L^2\) norm as \(\). We further determine the precise asymptotic behavior of the weak-type \((1,1)\) constant as \(n\to\infty\), yielding quantitative upper and lower bounds in terms of the dimension.
tldr: The paper establishes dimension-free L^p bounds and exact L^2 norm for the Littlewood-Paley g_alpha function associated with the fractional Poisson kernel, along with asymptotic weak-type (1,1) constants as dimension grows.
motivation: Littlewood-Paley g-functions are fundamental in harmonic analysis, and understanding their behavior with fractional Poisson kernels and dimension dependence is a natural extension of classical results.
method: The authors use harmonic analysis techniques, likely involving square function estimates, Calderón-Zygmund theory, and asymptotic analysis to derive bounds for the fractional Poisson kernel setting.
result: They obtain dimension-free L^p bounds for 1<p<∞, identify the exact L^2 norm, and provide quantitative upper and lower bounds for the weak-type (1,1) constant as n→∞.
conclusion: The work contributes precise norm estimates for Littlewood-Paley operators with fractional Poisson kernels, extending classical theory to the fractional case and clarifying dimension asymptotics.

title: Deep Learning Methods For Stochastic Galerkin Approximations Of Random Domain Problems
authors: Andrea Barth Fabio Musco
abstract: ArXiv:2609.32508v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work considers strong and weak stochastic Galerkin approximations of random domain problems for the elliptic random partial differential equation (PDE). The random domain problems are realized by sufficiently regular random domain mapping, allowing a transformation on deterministic reference domain. A traditional numerical method for solving the resulting high-dimensional coupled stochastic Galerkin systems is replaced by deep learning techniques. We compare a physics-informed neural network approach, based on the strong stochastic Galerkin residual, with a Deep Ritz approach, based on the weak stochastic Galerkin system, reformulated as Ritz energy minimization. The neural networks serve as surrogates for the deterministic spectral coefficients of the respective stochastic Galerkin solution. The stochastic parameters are not used as neural network input parameters and the stochastic domain is not sampled during training. The efficiency of the methods is demonstrated on a randomly stretched interval and a randomly deformed annulus in two spatial dimensions.
tldr: The paper replaces traditional high-dimensional stochastic Galerkin solvers for elliptic PDEs on random domains with physics-informed neural network and Deep Ritz surrogates for the spectral coefficients.
motivation: Random domain problems lead to high-dimensional coupled stochastic Galerkin systems that are computationally expensive to solve with conventional numerical methods.
method: A regular random domain mapping transforms the problem onto a deterministic reference domain; PINN (strong SG residual) and Deep Ritz (weak SG energy minimization) networks are then trained as surrogates for the deterministic spectral coefficients, without sampling the stochastic domain.
result: Both approaches are demonstrated on a randomly stretched interval and a randomly deformed annulus in two spatial dimensions, showing efficiency gains over traditional solvers.
conclusion: Deep learning surrogates offer a viable alternative for solving stochastic Galerkin systems arising from random domain elliptic PDE problems.

title: PDO-Split: A Real-Time Solver For Constrained Potential-Dominant Games
authors: Zhiyuan Zhang, Yue Guan, Panagiotis Tsiotras
abstract: ArXiv:2609.31936v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present Potential-Dominant Operator Splitting (PDO-Split), a real-time generalized Nash equilibrium solver for constrained dynamic multi-agent problems with potential-dominant structure. PDO-Split targets the computational bottleneck in game-theoretic model predictive control, where repeatedly solving the equilibrium KKT system becomes costly as the number of agents increases. We introduce a class of gamma-potential-dominant games, in which the potential (or cooperative) structure dominates the competitive interactions between the agents. We show that this structure allows PDO-Split to use the potential component as a preconditioner while incorporating the competitive component through iterative refinement. We establish convergence guarantees and exploit the symmetry of the potential component through a reusable LDL^T factorization to accelerate the linear solvers. We evaluate PDO-Split across several practical multi-agent planning problems, including eight-car racing and six-vehicle ramp merging, achieving substantially improved runtime and convergence rate over existing DDP-based and Newton-based methods, especially with a larger number of agents. The algorithm is also experimentally validated on miniature autonomous race car platforms, demonstrating the approach's real-time capability.
tldr: PDO-Split is a real-time solver for constrained potential-dominant generalized Nash equilibrium problems, applied to multi-agent planning and autonomous racing.
motivation: Game-theoretic model predictive control faces a computational bottleneck when repeatedly solving equilibrium KKT systems as the number of agents grows.
method: The paper introduces gamma-potential-dominant games and uses the potential component as a preconditioner while handling competitive interactions via iterative refinement, with a reusable LDL^T factorization exploiting symmetry.
result: PDO-Split achieves improved runtime and convergence rate over DDP-based and Newton-based methods on eight-car racing and six-vehicle ramp merging, and is validated on miniature autonomous race cars.
conclusion: The algorithm demonstrates real-time capability for constrained dynamic multi-agent problems with potential-dominant structure, but it is unrelated to quantum information science.

title: Connected Ef1 Allocations Exist In Discrete Chore Cutting
authors: Bo Li Ankang Sun
abstract: ArXiv:2609.32545v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove the existence of an envy-free up to one item (EF1) division for a discrete chore. Our approach builds on the powerful framework of Simmons-Su, which leverages Sperner's lemma to guarantee the existence of a simplex corresponding to a sequence of similar fractional divisions, ensuring that each agent is satisfied with a different bundle. Bil\`o et al. [2022] introduced a rounding technique that converts the fractional divisions into a connected integral EF1 division for goods when there are at most four agents, and this method was later extended by Igarashi [2023] to accommodate any number of agents. However, these rounding techniques for goods do not directly apply to chores because the definitions of EF1 differ in the two settings. To overcome this asymmetry, we modify the existing rounding techniques and show that connected EF1 divisions exist for a discrete chore.
tldr: The paper proves the existence of connected envy-free up to one item (EF1) allocations for discrete chore cutting by adapting fractional rounding techniques originally developed for goods.
motivation: Fair division of indivisible chores is less understood than goods, especially when connectivity constraints are required, and existing rounding techniques for goods do not directly apply due to asymmetric EF1 definitions.
method: The authors build on the Simmons-Su framework using Sperner's lemma and modify the Bilò et al./Igarashi rounding technique to handle the chore setting, overcoming the goods-chores asymmetry.
result: They establish that connected EF1 divisions always exist for any number of agents in discrete chore cutting.
conclusion: This resolves an open problem in fair division of chores and extends connectivity-constrained EF1 existence results from goods to chores.

title: Efficient And Adaptive Estimation Of Portfolio Weights With Spectral Risk Measures
authors: Ming Yuan Kangjie Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2609.31994v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spectral risk measures, including conditional value-at-risk (CVaR), generate a family of convex criteria for portfolio estimation. We study how the criterion should be chosen when different criteria share the same population minimizer, and whether the efficient criterion can itself be learned from data. We develop a general asymptotic theory for empirical spectral-risk minimization under estimated linear constraints. Under normal scale-mixture elliptical returns, all spectral risk measures identify the same population efficient portfolio, but their empirical minimizers have different sampling distributions. Their asymptotic covariance decomposes into a common component and a positive-semidefinite component scaled by a functional of the spectral measure, reducing efficiency to an optimization over probability measures. We characterize the efficiency-optimal spectral measure and show that single-level CVaR is generally inefficient. We then construct a fully data-adaptive estimator that learns the radial distribution and optimal spectral measure from the same observations used for portfolio estimation, yet has the same first-order distribution as the infeasible oracle. Simulations and an empirical application illustrate the method.
tldr: The paper develops asymptotic theory and a data-adaptive estimator for portfolio weights under spectral risk measures, showing single-level CVaR is generally inefficient and characterizing the efficiency-optimal spectral measure.
motivation: Different convex risk criteria (e.g., CVaR and other spectral risk measures) can share the same population efficient portfolio, so the choice of criterion is not innocuous; the authors ask how to pick and even learn the most statistically efficient criterion from data.
method: They derive a general asymptotic theory for empirical spectral-risk minimization under estimated linear constraints, decompose the asymptotic covariance into a common plus a spectral-measure-dependent positive-semidefinite component, and reduce efficiency to optimizing over probability measures, yielding a fully adaptive estimator.
result: Under normal scale-mixture elliptical returns, all spectral risk measures identify the same population efficient portfolio but differ in sampling distribution; the efficiency-optimal spectral measure is characterized, single-level CVaR is shown to be generally inefficient, and the adaptive estimator attains the infeasible oracle's first-order distribution.
conclusion: Criterion choice in spectral-risk portfolio estimation matters for statistical efficiency and can be learned adaptively from the same data used for estimation, as illustrated by simulations and an empirical application.

title: Very Sparse Return Sets In Arithmetic Dynamics
authors: She Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.32181v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When studying the dynamical Mordell-Lang conjecture by using the [MATH]-adic method, experts have found that return sets of the [MATH]-adic version of the DML problem can be very sparse. In this article, we investigate the similar phenomenon for a complex analytic version of the DML problem and the DML problem for backward orbits.
tldr: This paper studies very sparse return sets in dynamical Mordell-Lang problems for complex analytic and backward-orbit settings.
motivation: The dynamical Mordell-Lang conjecture and its p-adic method have revealed that return sets can be extremely sparse, motivating analogous investigations in complex analytic dynamics and for backward orbits.
method: The author investigates a complex analytic version of the dynamical Mordell-Lang problem and the problem for backward orbits, likely using techniques from arithmetic dynamics and complex analysis.
result: Sparse return sets are shown to occur in these analogous dynamical settings, extending the sparsity phenomenon beyond the p-adic case.
conclusion: The findings highlight that very sparse return sets are a broader feature of dynamical Mordell-Lang problems, not limited to the p-adic method.

title: Something To Talk About: Social Media As A Lens On Healthcare Ransomware Events
authors: Seoyoung Kweon, Paul Chung, Isabel Straw, Christian J. Dameff, Jeffrey L. Tully, Stefan Savage, Geoffrey M. Voelker, Deepak Kumar
abstract: ArXiv:2609.31984v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the modern era, ransomware attacks on critical healthcare organizations---like hospitals and insurers---are frequent, with impacts ranging from leaked private health information all the way to serious disruptions of urgent, time-sensitive clinical operations. Unfortunately, legal and economic incentives make it uncommon for hospitals to share basic information about these attacks, their scope, and the downstream impacts to patient care. In this paper, we explore the use of public social media posts---authored both by hospitals and by individuals---to garner more detailed insights about these attacks and their effects. We collect 1,628 Facebook and Reddit posts from 2018--2024, design and evaluate techniques to match post data to 212 ground-truth ransomware attacks, and conduct quantitative and qualitative analyses that explore the impacts such attacks have on critical hospital infrastructure, patient care, and providers. We conclude by discussing the promise and limitations of leveraging social data to study the impact of ransomware attacks and highlight areas of future research.
tldr: This paper analyzes social media posts to understand the impacts of ransomware attacks on healthcare organizations.
motivation: Hospitals often do not disclose details about ransomware attacks due to legal and economic incentives, so the authors explore public social media as an alternative data source.
method: They collect 1,628 Facebook and Reddit posts from 2018–2024, match them to 212 ground-truth ransomware attacks, and perform quantitative and qualitative analyses.
result: The analysis reveals insights into how ransomware attacks affect critical hospital infrastructure, patient care, and providers.
conclusion: The paper discusses the promise and limitations of using social data to study ransomware impacts and suggests future research directions.

title: Top Trading Cycles With Indifferences Under Matroid Constraints
authors: Yasushi Kawase
abstract: ArXiv:2609.32337v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the reallocation of indivisible objects among agents who may hold initial endowments and may be indifferent between objects. Each agent has her own set of admissible objects, and a matroid constraint specifies which combinations of assigned objects are feasible. The model contains the housing market, house allocation with newcomers who hold no endowment, and the assignment of students to schools under matroidal constraints at each school. For this model, we introduce the top-class trading cycles mechanism (TCTC), which extends the top trading cycles mechanism (TTC) to matroid constraints and weak preferences. When a trading cycle is selected, TCTC fixes each agent's top indifference class rather than a specific object and postpones the choice within the class to the end. TCTC is individually rational, Pareto efficient, and weakly group-strategy-proof on the full domain of weak preferences, and it runs in polynomial time. When preferences and reports are strict, TCTC is strongly group-strategy-proof. Together with a known impossibility result, our theorem establishes a maximal domain of school-by-school constraints for individual rationality, Pareto efficiency, and strategy-proofness.
tldr: The paper introduces the top-class trading cycles mechanism (TCTC) for reallocating indivisible objects under matroid constraints and weak preferences, extending top trading cycles to settings with indifferences.
motivation: Reallocation problems with initial endowments, indifferences, and feasibility constraints such as matroid constraints arise in housing markets, school choice, and assignment problems, where standard TTC does not directly apply.
method: The authors define TCTC, which fixes each agent's top indifference class rather than a specific object when selecting a trading cycle, and then resolve choices within the class at the end; they analyze its properties and complexity.
result: TCTC is individually rational, Pareto efficient, and weakly group-strategy-proof for weak preferences, runs in polynomial time, and becomes strongly group-strategy-proof under strict preferences and reports; together with an impossibility result, this establishes a maximal domain for school-by-school constraints.
conclusion: The work provides a mechanism that generalizes TTC to matroid-constrained reallocation with indifferences, achieving desirable efficiency and incentive properties on a maximal domain.

title: Characterising The Precision Of A Clock Without Any External Time Reference
authors: Pablo \'A. Dom\'inguez, Christopher Chubb, Mischa P. Woods
abstract: ArXiv:2609.31832v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Determining a clock's precision usually requires comparison with a better time reference, yet no ideal reference is physically attainable. We show how a single clock can characterise its own precision using only a signal splitter and delayed trigger, whose uncertainty is explicitly accounted for. The resulting estimator depends only on tick-count statistics. A purpose-built electronic circuit validates the method without an external timekeeper or a second clock.

title: Locality Of Kms States For Infinite Fermionic Lattice Systems
authors: Lennart Becker
abstract: ArXiv:2609.31858v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how thermal equilibrium states of infinite fermionic lattices respond to perturbations of the Hamiltonian. Our main result concerns extensive perturbations of a chosen KMS state. We show that exponential decay of correlations and exponential local indistinguishability under the extensive perturbation yield stretched-exponential decay of correlations for the perturbed state. Neither the initial nor the perturbed state is required to be unique, allowing stability to be studied in the presence of phase coexistence. Our approach uses Quantum Belief Propagation (QBP), which we establish directly on the underlying [MATH]-algebra. Combining QBP with Lieb--Robinson bounds, we show implications between decay of correlations, the principle that local perturbations perturb locally, and local indistinguishability, closing the cycle for perturbations of the tracial state under the stated decay, support and uniformity assumptions. For extensive perturbations under uniform clustering conditions, we also obtain a differentiable path of local equilibrium expectations and bound their change linearly in the interaction norm of the perturbation.

title: Local Determinant Defects And Low-Energy Subspace Stability In Semifinite Von Neumann Algebras
authors: Seyed Mahmoud Manjegani
abstract: ArXiv:2609.32095v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a finite-temperature test for the stability of low-energy spectral subspaces. The test uses a local determinant defect for the alpha-z Renyi kernel of two Gibbs states and bounds the tracial L2 distance between their low-energy projections. The main tool is a spectral-flattening principle for bounded positive injective operators in a semifinite von Neumann algebra. It reduces the local product defect to an exact two-projection formula. The thermal result applies to lower-bounded affiliated Hamiltonians with trace-class Gibbs operators and does not require the Hamiltonians to be close in operator norm. We give an infinite-level example with unbounded Hamiltonians. For matrices, the result gives a sum of principal-angle remainders. For qubits, the defect and the thermal gaps determine the ground-state overlap exactly. The same estimate gives a uniform error bound for bounded observables in an effective low-energy model. We also prove the determinant inequalities, their equality cases, and z-monotonicity in matrix, finite, and semifinite settings.
